title: Cities: Skylines | Power, Politics, & Planning: Episode 5: Public Housing Part 1
premise: donoteat01 argues that public housing outcomes follow funding, eligibility, racial discrimination, redevelopment, and maintenance policy rather than inherent moral failings of towers or residents.
coverage: An architectural slide lecture leads into a fictional clearance story and Pruitt–Igoe’s decline. Historical claims are the presenter’s. Cut times and sound-cue placement are approximate; brief transitions may be missed.

panels.heading: Opening: towers and title
panels.description: Red-brick game towers surround courts and parking. The episode title overlays the flyover before a white title card with the blue bird mascot.
panels.camera: The aerial view moves along the tower complex before the title graphic replaces it.
panels.action: Traffic is visible in the game; title graphics appear.

sound.text: Intro music: Brahms’s Tragic Overture, Op. 81, performed by the Musopen Symphony.

panels.heading: City builders omit public housing
panels.description: SimCity 2000 Select Arcology menu displays four futuristic structures and their prices/populations.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the ensuing clickbait municipal-factories insert: the serious omission of public housing in city-building games leads into an exaggerated title-card parody.

panels.heading: Clickbait state capitalism
panels.description: A thumbnail reads FACTS DON’T CARE ABOUT YOUR INDUSTRIES and DONOTEAT’S CLICKBAIT REVIEW, with a red arrow and emoji decorations.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: An aggressively decorated self-promotional clickbait parody intrudes on the municipal-factories explanation.

panels.heading: Stigma setup: gang stereotype
panels.description: A photograph of a tattooed back replaces the game view.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The visual literalizes the absurd claim that public housing residents are all gang members.

panels.heading: Stigma escalation: ISIS
panels.description: The tattoo image is joined by a photograph of armed men with black ISIS flags.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The montage escalates from gang panic to terrorism, ridiculing the narration’s exaggerated stereotype.

panels.heading: Paint conspiracy setup
panels.description: Oxycodone blister packs appear against black.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The pills literalize the absurd drug-osmosis explanation; the image shows prescription tablets rather than heroin.

panels.heading: Paint conspiracy payoff
panels.description: Alex Jones sits at an INFOWARS LIVE desk.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Cutting from drugs to Infowars gives the ridiculous government-mind-control story a recognizable conspiracy-media punchline.

panels.heading: Two-part agenda
panels.description: HOPE VI appears over close game views of the red-brick towers.
panels.camera: The game camera travels past the tower facades under the HOPE VI overlay.
panels.action: No depicted residents; traffic remains background action.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the subsequent celebrity collage: the serious Part 2 agenda proceeds from privatization and HOPE VI to Section 8, Kanye West and Elon Musk, introducing an intentionally incongruous teaser.

panels.heading: Kanye and Lil Pump box-costume teaser
panels.description: An oversized image of Kanye West and Lil Pump wearing box-shaped costumes in a pink-lit corridor covers much of the game freeway view.
panels.camera: Static costume photograph over a changing freeway view.
panels.action: The two men pose in giant costumes in a still photograph.
panels.visualGag: The celebrity punchline to the preceding affordable-housing/Section 8 agenda is literalized with the incongruous I Love It costume image. This sets up the added Musk-smoking inset in the next panel.

panels.heading: Musk-smoking inset escalates the collage
panels.description: The Kanye/Lil Pump costume image remains behind a newly added lower-right photograph of Elon Musk smoking beside a podcast microphone.
panels.camera: A smaller static photograph is added over the costume image.
panels.action: Musk holds something lit, with visible smoke.
panels.visualGag: Payoff/escalation of the previous box-costume insert: the second celebrity mentioned in the Part 2 teaser receives a familiar incongruous meme image atop the first. Neither image documents actual housing tenants.

panels.heading: Celebrity collage clears; history resumes
panels.description: The freeway and red-brick game towers are unobscured again; the celebrity overlays have cleared.
panels.camera: Return from inserted photographs to game-city framing.
panels.action: Background traffic remains; no photographed celebrities are present.
panels.visualGag: Closes the preceding Kanye/Lil Pump plus Musk collage sequence, returning from the absurd celebrity teaser to the serious history-and-architecture lecture setup.

panels.heading: Get the projector
panels.description: A photograph of a slide projector overlays the game city.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The imaginary graduate-student request receives a literal equipment insert.

panels.heading: Almshouses
panels.description: A historical drawing of low buildings appears within a rounded, projected-slide border.
panels.camera: The slide appears blurred, sharpens, then holds.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Payoff/continuation of the preceding projector photograph: the simulated slide arrives blurred then sharpens, sustaining the imaginary graduate-student lecture staging.
panels.notes: The rounded border and the blur mimic a real slide projector.

panels.heading: Punitive workhouses
panels.description: Brick institutional entrance bears ERECTED A.D.1854; the workhouse account describes labor and less eligibility.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Worse than life outside
panels.description: A historical bird’s-eye drawing shows a walled institutional complex, holding while the narrator explains Victorian poverty.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Howard’s alternative
panels.description: A black-and-white mustached portrait accompanies the introduction of Ebenezer Howard.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Garden City diagram
panels.description: Green-tinted concentric/radial diagram shows connected settlements; the presenter cautions against reading it literally.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Letchworth’s compromise
panels.description: Aerial photograph of a leafy town illustrates the built Garden City, while the presenter explains how private investment displaced cooperative principles.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Central thesis
panels.description: The slide reads ARCHITECTURE ALONE CANNOT SOLVE SOCIAL PROBLEMS.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

sound.text: “Le Corbusier” gets a poor French pronunciation, the first of eleven in the lecture.

panels.heading: Corbusier biography setup
panels.description: A black-and-white full-length portrait of Le Corbusier in round spectacles sets up the rapid biography; the narration names him.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the rapid blah-blah architecture montage, which moves from conventional architectural achievements to the Vichy-collaborator punchline.

sound.text: “Villa Savoye” gets a poor French pronunciation as the house flashes past.

panels.heading: Villa Savoye
panels.description: The rapid slide montage briefly shows a white modernist house raised on columns.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Its very brief appearance participates in the spoken blah-blah dismissal of a standard architecture lecture.
panels.notes: The slide is initially blurred by the projector effect.

panels.heading: Towards a New Architecture
panels.description: A book cover reads VERS UNE ARCHITECTURE.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: A rapid scholarly checklist continues rather than a detailed account of the book.

panels.heading: Machine-for-living and Modulor montage
panels.description: The rapid montage reaches a blurred human-proportion drawing with seated and standing bodies and a raised arm, apparently related to the Modulor.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The proportion diagram continues the dismissive blah-blah Corbusier biography before the Vichy-collaboration image.
panels.notes: The diagram looks like the Modulor, though that is not certain.

sound.text: “Vichy” gets a poor French pronunciation just before the collaboration image.

panels.heading: Vichy collaborator punchline
panels.description: A street photograph shows a building-sized antisemitic exhibition poster reading LE JUIF ET LA FRANCE.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The biography ends on collaboration imagery instead of architectural achievement.
panels.notes: The antisemitic propaganda image is there to indict Vichy collaboration. It does not by itself prove the claim about Corbusier.

sound.text: Another poor French pronunciation of “Le Corbusier.”
“Unité d’Habitation” gets a poor French pronunciation.

panels.heading: Radiant City
panels.description: Black-and-white model/plan image shows repeated cruciform towers amid a road grid.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

sound.text: “Le Corbusier” again, in poor French pronunciation.

panels.heading: Upside-down slide setup
panels.description: The Unité facade photograph appears inverted, with sky below the building.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The simulated lecture makes the slide-projector operator put the building upside down; the presenter asks to flip it.

panels.heading: Upside-down slide payoff
panels.description: The same colorful-balcony facade is upright, sky above.
panels.camera: The orientation is abruptly corrected; the photograph then holds.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The visibly corrected orientation pays off the request to flip the slide.

sound.text: The shortened “Corbusier” gets a poor French pronunciation.
“Vichy” comes back with the same poor French pronunciation.
“Unité d’Habitation” again, in poor French pronunciation.
The shortened “Unité” gets a poor French pronunciation.

panels.heading: Architecture-to-policy pivot
panels.description: Aerial historical image of rows of slab towers replaces the Unité photograph.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

sound.text: A final poor French pronunciation of “Unité.”

panels.heading: Two successful precedents
panels.description: Karl-Marx-Hof facade and Greenbelt commercial-center photographs introduce the municipal examples.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Social Democrats setup
panels.description: Red three-arrow emblem with SOCIAL DEMOCRATS caption replaces the architecture images.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the Rosa portrait interruption: the narrator anticipates audience objections to learning from the Social Democrats before showing the portrait and asking them to shut up.

panels.heading: Rosa interruption
panels.description: A black-and-white portrait of Rosa Luxemburg interrupts the party emblem, then the emblem returns; the narration names her.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The visual aside matches the presenter’s anticipation of objections about Rosa’s killing.
panels.notes: The portrait carries no name; the narration says “Rosa.”

panels.heading: Capital flight
panels.description: Aerial Vienna imagery descends toward the red-roofed complex; CAPITAL FLIGHT is overlaid.
panels.camera: The view zooms from a citywide map to an oblique view of the building.
panels.action: Geographic framing changes; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Low rents as material gains
panels.description: Oblique views trace red-roofed courtyard blocks and a large arched frontage.
panels.camera: Aerial views move along and around the courtyard complex, alternating facade and overhead angles.
panels.action: No character action; built form and courtyard scale are the subject.

panels.heading: Tax-funded upkeep
panels.description: Overhead view follows the long courtyard complex, then pulls away from its monumental front.
panels.camera: A near-overhead pass along the complex changes to a facade view, then pulls back.
panels.action: No depicted character action.
panels.visualGag: The end of the housing-funding section introduces the Resettlement Administration, or RA, setting up the masked-gunmen insert about the other RA.

panels.heading: Not the other RA
panels.description: A black-and-white photograph of masked armed men overlays the Vienna aerial.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The armed-men insert resolves the spoken RA acronym joke toward the IRA rather than the New Deal housing agency.
panels.notes: The photo carries no organization label; the IRA reading comes from context.

panels.heading: Greenbelt
panels.description: Leafy low-rise blocks, community facilities, pool, and streets fill moving aerial imagery.
panels.camera: The aerial view glides across facilities and wooded housing, then rises to wider views.
panels.action: No visible tenant actions; the narrative supplies the rules and cooperative governance.

panels.heading: Buying homes is un-American
panels.description: A historical committee/hearing-room photograph interrupts Greenbelt.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The insert supplies HUAC’s institutional punchline to residents supposedly becoming suspect for buying their own homes.

panels.heading: Pretty good
panels.description: Centered white text on black reads “PRETTY GOOD”.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Understated two-word verdict replaces the monumental housing tour after the elaborate case studies.

panels.heading: What is a slum?
panels.description: A photograph of people standing among rubble between tenements accumulates OLD, RUN-DOWN HOUSING / OVERCROWDING / NO RUNNING WATER / SLUMLORDS.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: First room to himself
panels.description: Gil Scott-Heron Pieces of a Man cover sits beside lyrics concluding that jail supplied a first private room.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Oldest trick, literal book
panels.description: THE OLDEST TRICK IN THE BOOK appears above a worn old book.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Literalizing the idiom with an actual aged book makes the policy lecture briefly a visual pun.

panels.heading: Two budgets
panels.description: THE CAPITAL BUDGET AND THE OPERATIONS BUDGET introduces images of towers and a large Carrier chiller.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Capital gets the glory
panels.description: Text lists BIG CONTRACT AWARDS / RIBBON CUTTINGS / STUFF POLITICIANS LIKE beneath THE CAPITAL BUDGET.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the next operations-budget janitor insert: contracts and ribbon cuttings flatter politicians, then the reclining cartoon janitor reduces upkeep to an unglamorous punchline.

panels.heading: Operations gets the janitor
panels.description: THE OPERATIONS BUDGET sits above Scruffy, the reclining mustached janitor from Futurama.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The pop-culture janitor insert contrasts mundane upkeep with glamorous capital spending.
panels.notes: Scruffy is the Futurama janitor; the source episode is unknown.

panels.heading: Oldest book callback
panels.description: An aged book appears beneath THE OLDEST TRICK IN THE BOOK, repeating the earlier literal illustration of the idiom.
panels.action: The book card replaces the cartoon operations-budget janitor, then gives way to the budget-sabotage formula.
panels.visualGag: Callback to the earlier oldest-trick book image: the repeated idiom is again literalized with a visibly old book, linking the janitor budget comparison to deliberate underfunding.

panels.heading: The sabotage formula
panels.description: FUND THE CAPITAL BUDGET IN FULL / BUT / INSIST THAT OPERATIONS ARE SELF-SUFFICIENT summarizes the mechanism.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Fiat currency pun
panels.description: A small white Fiat car appears during the fiat-currency explanation.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: An automobile brand literally substitutes for the monetary adjective; next insert switches to printing money.

panels.heading: Selective deficit anxiety
panels.description: Defense-company logos give way to a national debt clock as the presenter contrasts military financing with social-service austerity.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: We just pay for it
panels.description: A card reads “HOW DO WE PAY FOR IT?” / WE JUST PAY FOR IT.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Verbal setup for the immediate Matt Lesko FREE MONEY image: the government-funding answer tees up the unexpected endorsement of the flamboyant free-money promoter.

panels.heading: Matt Lesko was right
panels.description: Question-mark-suit promoter and FREE MONEY book cover fill the screen.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The garish free-money pitch becomes an unexpected approving payoff to the government-funding argument.

panels.heading: The labor housing coalition
panels.description: Hosiery workers, an architect/building pairing, Catherine Bauer’s portrait and MODERN HOUSING book, then a union label establish the coalition.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.notes: Catherine Bauer’s name is visible on the book. The architect’s surname is uncertain.

panels.heading: Replacement instead of addition
panels.description: EVERY PUBLIC UNIT CONSTRUCTED REQUIRED A PRIVATE UNIT TO BE DEMOLISHED cuts to an overhead game neighborhood; SLUM CLEARANCE cards follow.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: 1949 clearance for developers
panels.description: Photographs of large urban developments follow HOUSING ACT OF 1949, before the acquisition-process text.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Contractor delay setup and payoff
panels.description: A numbered acquisition/building slide ends WHO WILL BUILD THE PROJECT… and later adds …EVENTUALLY.
panels.action: Text is added; otherwise static slide.
panels.visualGag: The delayed extra word converts a neutral process chart into a joke about contractors collecting rent before building.

panels.heading: Intermission
panels.description: INTERMISSION holds on black for the announced break.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the literal vintage lobby-cartoon musical intermission: a request to let premiere viewers get snacks is followed by the snack song and anthropomorphic refreshments.

panels.heading: Let’s all go to the lobby
panels.description: Animated refreshments march across a cinema scene, followed by a family eating snacks and a concession counter.
panels.camera: Fixed-frame inset cartoon that changes shots as the refreshments march and the family eats.
panels.action: Anthropomorphic snack packages walk; cartoon family eats and drinks.
panels.visualGag: A real vintage theatrical intermission cartoon literalizes the offer to fetch food during a YouTube premiere.

sound.text: “Let’s All Go to the Lobby” accompanies the marching refreshments and snack break.

panels.heading: Return to 52nd Street
panels.description: Lobby lyric card ends; after INTERMISSION, the game returns to intact rows of low-rise houses.
panels.camera: Cut from the intermission card to an oblique view of the game neighborhood, which then pulls back.
panels.action: Traffic moves through the intact neighborhood.
panels.visualGag: The lobby-song refrain carries over for a few seconds to finish the intermission; the return to the housing story is played straight.

sound.text: The lobby-song refrain continues over the closing lyric card before the narrator resumes.

panels.heading: Two kinds of slum
panels.description: The second definition reads ANYTHING DEVELOPERS FIND CONVENIENT TO CALL A SLUM below the conventional definition.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Mrs. O’Leary’s stakes
panels.description: Highlighted row house is labeled with widowhood, two cats, paid mortgage, rental/Social Security retirement, and COMPENSATION: $50,000 AND A SECTION 8 VOUCHER.
panels.camera: The overhead game camera zooms from the district to her house, then holds for the labels.
panels.action: House is selected; character and cats are not actually shown.

panels.heading: Clearance boundary
panels.description: A translucent red rectangle marks the project area; a red arrow points into it.
panels.camera: Fixed overhead view with added area overlay.
panels.action: Graphic boundary and arrow appear.

panels.heading: Progress Realty Partners
panels.description: Blue PRP corporate logo, Wilmington address, and small building photograph replace the game view.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: An ordinary-looking address photograph accompanies the spoken claim that hundreds of thousands of corporations share it; shell-company satire is supplied by the narration.

panels.heading: Year 3: pressure to evict
panels.description: JUNE, YEAR 3 leads back to the game; “HUMANELY RELOCATE” then receives a standalone card.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Scare quotes set up the contradiction between humane language and the coercive process that follows.

panels.heading: Rents correction
panels.description: A small *RENTS caption appears at bottom right of the neighborhood view.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.notes: Corrects the spoken “rates”; it doesn’t read as a joke.

panels.heading: Relocation office
panels.description: The fixed neighborhood overview remains intact while narration recounts irregular office access and the $800 offer.
panels.camera: Fixed overhead game view; no depicted office interior.
panels.action: No visible Mrs. O’Leary or office interaction; these actions are spoken only.

panels.heading: Bad housing montage setup
panels.description: A SpongeBob SquarePants settlement of repeated blue cylindrical houses appears.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Cartoon underwater housing replaces the real relocation market as the account describes unacceptable alternatives.

panels.heading: Bad housing montage escalation
panels.description: Patrick Star’s rock house from SpongeBob SquarePants, under a weather vane, fills the screen.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Patrick’s rock-like dwelling shows how unsuitable the relocation options are.

panels.heading: Bad housing montage payoff
panels.description: Squidward Tentacles’ stone-head house and SpongeBob’s pineapple house stand beside Patrick Star’s rock in SpongeBob SquarePants.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The montage finishes with absurd Bikini Bottom dwellings instead of credible city apartments; no tenant is shown moving there.

panels.heading: December, year 3
panels.description: Date card gives way to bulldozer UI and CONFIRM DEMOLITION over the neighborhood.
panels.camera: Fixed overhead game framing; modal overlay dims the background.
panels.action: A building is selected for demolition; subsequent frames show missing buildings.

panels.heading: First relocation and clearances
panels.description: Red arrow identifies the next occupied building beside growing brown cleared plots.
panels.camera: The overhead view holds as buildings are removed one after another.
panels.action: Rows of buildings disappear and brown paving or bare ground fills the cleared sites. The failed heating in the narration is not shown.

panels.heading: Repair promise
panels.description: A standalone “SOON” card interrupts the demolition view.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Scare-quoted promise lands as the presenter says the broken window will never be repaired.

panels.heading: July, year 4
panels.description: Date card returns to the same neighborhood; cleared ground borders surviving row houses.
panels.camera: Fixed overhead framing; the resident’s move is not animated.
panels.action: The visual tracks the shrinking housing stock, not interior disrepair.

panels.heading: September and December moves
panels.description: New tower footprints appear on cleared land; arrows relocate attention among surviving row houses.
panels.camera: Overhead framing remains fixed while date cards cut in.
panels.action: Game placement creates tower blocks; arrows indicate narrated moves without a visible walking character.

panels.heading: March and June, year 5
panels.description: Arrows point toward surviving properties amid towers; date cards advance the story.
panels.action: More buildings are removed; Mrs. O’Leary’s boxed possessions and kitchen toilet are not pictured.

panels.heading: An exceptionally lucky ending
panels.description: Finished brick towers and blue courts fill an oblique flyover, replacing the demolition UI.
panels.camera: Cut from the overhead construction interface to an oblique camera travelling along and around the completed towers.
panels.action: Traffic is visible; no apartment interior or resident is shown.

panels.heading: What just happened?
panels.description: WHAT JUST HAPPENED? overlays replayed clearance imagery; Robert Moses’s portrait briefly covers the game; the final card says YA GOT SCREWED.
panels.camera: Fixed overhead replay with inserted portrait and text cuts.
panels.action: Demolition and tower placement recur in the explanation; the replay is not another distinct chronology.

panels.heading: Pruitt–Igoe case
panels.description: Aerial present-day imagery traces a wooded site; historical low houses appear with new towers in the background.
panels.camera: Oblique geographic camera circles the site before a hard cut to historical stills.
panels.action: No character action in the historical photograph.

panels.heading: Modern homes, now an empty site
panels.description: The Pruitt-Igoe Myth poster interrupts the map; the geographic view then rises over a large wooded rectangle.
panels.camera: Zooms out from the wooded site.
panels.action: The site appears without its former towers, giving away the ending in advance.

panels.heading: Racially restricted suburbs
panels.description: Historical suburb aerial cuts to a sign reading WE WANT WHITE TENANTS IN OUR WHITE COMMUNITY.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.notes: A real racist sign, used as serious illustration rather than a gag.

panels.heading: Built for growth
panels.description: Construction photograph gives way to a clean finished slab facade, illustrating the project before decline.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Eligibility as a plan-level problem
panels.description: A Pruitt–Igoe site plan pans through black building footprints and roads.
panels.camera: The view slides across the static plan.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Families under inspection
panels.description: Historical photograph shows children in a bright window-lined gallery, contrasting with the narration’s intrusive eligibility rules.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.notes: Hiding fathers is narrated, not shown.

panels.heading: Blaming families
panels.description: Article headlines accumulate, including How Liberal Policies Destroyed Black Families and contrary accounts of blame directed at single parents.
panels.action: Headline images are layered successively; no character action.

panels.heading: The operating-budget trap returns
panels.description: Historical aerial of the development cuts to a weathered facade with broken/dark windows as occupancy and maintenance decline.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Vandal-proof
panels.description: Standalone “VANDAL-PROOF” card punctuates the lighting-fixture story.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Scare quotes undercut a supposed technical fix that the presenter says was costlier and more tempting to vandals.

panels.heading: Tenant resistance
panels.description: Aerial development photograph cuts to a woman speaking among seated people as Bertha Gilkey and the rent strike are discussed.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.notes: The image carries no label; the narration identifies Gilkey.

panels.heading: Demolition becomes the memory
panels.description: A black-and-white photograph captures towers collapsing in a cloud of dust.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.notes: The collapse is a still photograph.

panels.heading: Counterexample: New York
panels.description: Aerial tour of repeating multi-wing apartment blocks broadens to the surrounding waterfront street grid.
panels.camera: The view pulls upward and rotates.
panels.action: No tenants are shown.

panels.heading: Inhuman proportions setup
panels.description: Red arrow points at a tall tower in a street photograph.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: The image sets up the ridiculous claim that a high-floor apartment turns its occupant into a monster.

panels.heading: Inhuman proportions comparison
panels.description: Red arrow points at a two-story row house in a different photograph.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.
panels.visualGag: Ordinary low-rise housing completes the visual comparison; no literal monster transformation is shown.

panels.heading: Material answer
panels.description: SMALL BUILDINGS ARE EASIER AND CHEAPER TO MAINTAIN appears as the substantive replacement for moral architectural explanations.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Maintenance systems
panels.description: Elevator-bank photo, wheelchair-access symbol, sprinkler, water tower, and industrial incinerator illustrate the cost comparison.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Height raises repair costs
panels.description: Boom lift on grass cuts to a high-rise facade with suspended work platforms.
panels.action: Static image; no visible character action.

panels.heading: Eyes on the street
panels.description: EYES ON THE STREET card cuts to game low-rise homes and courts.
panels.camera: The aerial view circles low-rise housing and neighboring row-house blocks.
panels.action: No depicted corridor or elevator encounter; the safety examples are narrated.

panels.heading: Fully funded homes and Part 2
panels.description: Game aerial low-rise development remains amid older rows of housing as the presenter concludes and previews privatization.
panels.camera: An oblique orbit turns into an overhead sideways traverse.
panels.action: Traffic in the city; no character performance.

panels.heading: Thanks and channel updates
